messages:
maria (Finance): Hey team — FYI we just shipped AcmeCorp's monthly invoice (INV-2026-03-AC) and several expected line items are missing (reserved capacity and overage rows).
maria (Finance): The invoice total is also lower than the usage report by ~$12k. Customer called, they flagged it. Can someone check the generation job?
dan (Billing): I can take a look. Do we have the invoice generation job id or the run id from the billing pipeline?
maria (Finance): Job id from the UI: job_2026_03_1746. I also attached a PDF in the thread (screenshot pasted). The summary section only shows subscription charge, no per-model usage lines.
invoice-bot: invoice-generator | job_2026_03_1746 | status: completed_with_warnings. warning: "line_item_count_mismatch=2" (see logs)
dan (Billing): Hmm warning suggests template vs computed items mismatch. Olivia/olga — did any recent template changes land on master last night?
olga (Finance Ops): I merged a microfix for address formatting but didn't touch line item templates. I can pull the template diff and compare.
sachin (Account Exec): Acme is asking for an updated invoice asap. They're withholding payment until it's reconciled. Can we expedite?
dan (Billing): I'll re-run the generation job in staging with the same inputs and attach the raw JSON payload we send to the renderer.
aj (Eng SRE): tagging in case there's a downstream renderer issue. invoice-renderer service had a deploy 03:10 UTC yesterday. Any correlation with beginning-of-month runs?
dan (Billing): Re-run result: renderer returned 200 but payload_items.length=4 while final_pdf.items_rendered=2. Possible post-render pruning step dropped rows.
maria (Finance): Do we have the raw calculation that produced the 4 items (usage details)? I can attach them to the customer email if we need to show the breakdown.
dan (Billing): raw_items JSON:
```
[{"code":"reserved_gpu_monthly","desc":"Reserved capacity - A100","amount":12000},{"code":"gpu_usage_overage","desc":"Spot overage","amount":3000},{"code":"embeddings_units","desc":"Embeddings (prod)","amount":450},{"code":"support_addon","desc":"Priority support","amount":200}]
```
invoice-bot: renderer | job_2026_03_1746 | post_render_hook: removed 2 empty-description rows
aj (Eng SRE): Looking at logs now — the post_render cleanup uses a heuristic that dropped items with desc length < 4 after templating. That heuristic is from a 2024 hotfix that was supposed to trim blank metadata. It looks like templating produced short desc for two items due to escaping bug.
olga (Finance Ops): Which items got short desc? Can we map codes?
dan (Billing): It appears gpu_usage_overage and embeddings_units got their desc collapsed because of an embedded newline in the description field during template substitution.
maria (Finance): That matches the customer's report — they expect the overage rows. Can we generate a corrected invoice and send a credit/updated PDF before EOD?
aj (Eng SRE): I'll revert the cleanup heuristic on the renderer in staging and push a fix to production if tests pass. Need a billing signoff to trigger hotfix.
sachin (Account Exec): Please proceed — Acme is high priority (enterprise sales). Keep me in loop.
dan (Billing): Creating a corrected invoice now by re-running with the raw_items and forcing bypass of post_render cleanup: job_2026_03_1746_fix.
invoice-bot: invoice-generator | job_2026_03_1746_fix | status: completed. invoice_id: INV-2026-03-AC-v2. PDF URL: https://invoices.redwood.ai/INV-2026-03-AC-v2.pdf
maria (Finance): Reviewed v2 — all 4 line items present and totals reconcile to usage report. Sending to Acme with apology + note about updated invoice and no change to billing period (just corrected formatting).
olga (Finance Ops): Filing a follow-up to add a unit test for newline-handling in billing template substitutions.
aj (Eng SRE): Patch shipped to prod to stop aggressive post-render pruning. Monitor for any other invoices affected tonight.
sachin (Account Exec): Thanks team. I'll notify Acme and confirm they're unblocked.
maria (Finance): Closing this thread once payment clears. :thumbsup:
